findings.title: Cleanup service ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1` (likely left over from local debugging), while `srv.clean` still uses `const timeout = 9 * time.Minute`. This causes all background cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, and query history) to run 10x more frequently than intended.

findings.title: Leftover debug `r.log.Error` calls log every cleanup batch as an error with full ID slices
findings.body: `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579) call `r.log.Error` unconditionally on every batch iteration, even when `err` is `nil`, and include the full `ids` slice in the log fields. Because `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` can be thousands of IDs, this will emit large error-level log entries on every batch of every cleanup run.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is constructed in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. Because strings are immutable in Go, re-formatting `values` on each iteration copies the entire accumulated string every time, taking O(N^2) time and allocations (for example, ~32k iterations in the new test case allocate hundreds of megabytes). Building the list with `strings.Builder` and `strconv.AppendInt` avoids the quadratic allocation.
